newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize futures down, new wheat up in busy Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Maize futures down, new wheat up in busy Budapest.

text.p: Speculative trade in Budapest Commodity Exchange new (1997) crop milling wheat futures) reversed a three-day downward trend, traders said on Friday.
"The price rose on speculation, belying market expectations of further falls," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap.
August milling wheat rose 300 forints per tonne to 21,500 forints, while September went up the daily limit ofd 400 forints per tonne to end at 21,900.
July, October and December remained steady and May dropped 300 forints to 24,000.
The milling wheat price increase triggered limit rises in new crop feed barley for July and August to 18,000 and 18,500 forints respectively.
Maize futures continued their downward movement, although at a slower pace then during the last three days.
May was the only maize maturity that was unchanged, at 17,540 forints, while others finished 40 to 100 forints lower.

Total turnover was 1,778 contracts or 736.83 million forints, a substantial amount for a traditionally slow Friday trade, with milling wheat accounting for 965 contracts. Lot size = 20,000 kgs ($1=177.45 Hungarian forints)
